extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive/ procedural requirements for filing, converting, and claiming benefit/priority for provisional, nonprovisional, divisional, continuation, and continuation-in-part patent applications before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a), and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a). A cover sheet required by 37 CFR 1.51(c)(1) must be included, which may be an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76), the Office's form SB/16, or a cover letter identifying the application as a provisional application. The parts required are set forth in 37 CFR 1.51(c) and MPEP § 601.01(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment other than to make the provisional application comply with the patent statute and regulations may be made after the filing date. Although the application will be accorded a filing date regardless of whether any drawings are submitted, applicants are advised to file any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a) with the application. A provisional application disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences is not required to include a separate sequence listing; however, if submitted in a provisional application filed on or after July 1, 2022, any submission of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence data must be by way of a 'Sequence Listing XML' in compliance with §§ 1.831 through 1.834.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of a provisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a), and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a), are filed in the Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For provisional applications filed on or after December 18, 2013, the filing date is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a), with or without claims, is filed. The filing date is accorded regardless of whether drawings are submitted, but applicants are advised to submit required drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No claims, oath, or declaration required in provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim, and an inventor's oath or declaration, are not required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: (A) No claim is required in a provisional application. (B) No oath or declaration is required in a provisional application. (C) Provisional applications will not be examined for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12‑month pendency and abandonment of provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application will automatically be abandoned 12 months after its filing date and will not be subject to revival after such 12‑month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period of pendency is extended to the next succeeding business day if the 12‑month anniversary falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday. Example dates are provided. Effective December 18, 2013, a nonprovisional filed more than 12 months but within 14 months after the provisional's filing date may have the benefit restored by filing a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of a nonprovisional to a provisional (and vice versa) — timing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) may be converted to a provisional application if a request and fee (37 CFR 1.17(q)) are submitted prior to the earlier of abandonment, payment of issue fee, or expiration of 12 months after the filing date. Likewise, a provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application if a request (with fee 37 CFR 1.17(i)) and required amendment(s) are filed prior to the earlier of abandonment or expiration of 12 months after the provisional filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant of such a conversion request will not entitle applicant to a refund of fees properly paid. Conversion of a provisional to a nonprovisional will result in the term of any patent issuing from the application being measured from at least the filing date of the provisional application (adverse patent term impact). Applicants are advised to consider claiming the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) rather than converting to avoid this impact. The nonprovisional resulting from conversion must include the filing, search, and examination fees, the inventor's oath or declaration, and any surcharge under 1.16(f) if appropriate; an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) is required unless the provisional already contained at least one such claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications not entitled to priority/benefit of earlier applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is not entitled to the right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119, 365(a), or 386(a) or to the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), nor to certain provisions in 37 CFR (e.g., §1.55, §1.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No claim for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or §1.78(a) may be made in a design application based on a provisional application. If applicant attempts to claim the benefit of an earlier U.S. application or priority to a foreign application in a provisional application, the filing receipt will not reflect the improper benefit or priority claim. If a nonprovisional attempts to claim benefit earlier than the provisional's filing date, the claim will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submissions in provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences is not required to include a separate sequence listing; however, if submitted in a provisional application filed on or after July 1, 2022, sequence data must be submitted as a 'Sequence Listing XML' in compliance with §§1.831–1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of §§1.821–1.825 regarding application disclosures containing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences are not mandatory for provisional applications (except for XML requirement for filings on/after July 1, 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and consequences of nonpayment/timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee may be submitted after the specification and any required drawing are submitted, within such period and under such conditions, including payment of a surcharge, as prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon failure to submit the fee within the prescribed period, the application shall be regarded as abandoned unless it is shown to the satisfaction of the Director that the delay was unavoidable or unintentional. For nonprovisional applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, basic filing, search, examination and application size fees and the inventor's oath or declaration are required for a complete application but may be filed after the application filing date upon payment of the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference requirements when claiming benefit of prior applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nonprovisional (or international filings entering national stage) that claims the benefit of one or more prior-filed nonprovisional/international applications/design applications must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each such prior-filed application identifying it by application number, international application number and filing date, or registration number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference must also identify the relationship of the applications (continuation, divisional, continuation‑in‑part). If the later-filed application is a nonprovisional application, the reference must be included in an application data sheet (§1.76(b)(5)). An application claiming the benefit of a provisional under 35 U.S.C.119(e) should not be called a 'divisional' of the provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application substantive and formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application is a later application for an independent or distinct invention carved out of a nonprovisional (including those from international applications) that discloses and claims only subject matter disclosed in the earlier or parent application. The divisional should set forth at least the portion of the earlier disclosure that is germane to the invention as claimed in the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The divisional must not include subject matter which would constitute new matter if submitted as an amendment to the parent application. A divisional may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or 1.53(d) if a design application, but not an international design application). The inventorship in the divisional must include at least one inventor named in the prior-filed application and must claim the benefit of the prior-filed application under 35 U.S.C.120,121,365(c), or 386(c). Divisional applications are often filed as a result of a restriction requirement. A continuation‑in‑part should not be designated as a divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship overlap and correction for divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship in the divisional application must include at least one inventor named in the prior-filed application; where restriction requires change, inventorship may need correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application by joint inventors includes more than one independent and distinct invention and restriction is required, it may be necessary to change inventorship named in the application if the elected invention is not the invention of all originally named joint inventors. The examiner should remind applicants of necessity to correct inventorship pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 if claims to an inventor are canceled. Inventorship overlap need not be present at the time the continuing application is filed nor when the parent issues or becomes abandoned if the parent prior to restriction names the inventor or a joint inventor of the divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional design application rules (design from utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A design application may be considered to be a divisional of a utility application and entitled to the filing date thereof if the drawings of the earlier filed utility application show the same article as that in the design application sufficiently to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a divisional design application may only be filed under the procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(b), and not under 37 CFR 1.53(d). See MPEP § 1504.20 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter may be introduced after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to nonprovisional applications; continuing applications (continuation, divisional, continuation‑in‑part) may be filed under the conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) and §1.78. A continuation‑in‑part may disclose and claim subject matter not disclosed in the prior application, whereas a divisional may not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules for nonprovisional applications (post‑Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after December 18, 2013, the filing date of a nonprovisional application (other than a design patent application) is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office. Utility and plant patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) are no longer required to include at least one claim or any drawings to receive a filing date. The filing date of a design patent application is the date on which the specification including at least one claim and any required drawings are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective December 18, 2013, a nonprovisional application may be filed by a reference to a previously filed application indicating that the specification and any drawings of the application are replaced by the reference to the previously filed application (per 35 U.S.C. 111(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and filing paragraphs for continuation/divisional/CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.53(b) is the section under which almost all applications are filed except certain special cases (entry of international application, provisional under 1.53(c), continued prosecution application (CPA) of a design application under 1.53(d), or a nonprovisional international design application). A continuation, divisional, or CIP may be filed under conditions specified in the statutes and 37 CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuation or divisional naming the same or fewer inventors may be filed under paragraph (b) or (d). A continuation‑in‑part or a continuation/divisional naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under paragraph (c). Applications filed under 1.53(b) will be treated as filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 2.01 — possible status as divisional (examiner practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 2.01 to remind applicant of possible divisional status: the application appears to claim only subject matter directed to an invention that is independent and distinct from that claimed in the prior application and names the inventor or at least one joint inventor named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: insert application number and filing date of the prior application in brackets. This form paragraph should be used only if it appears the application may be a divisional but a benefit claim has not been properly established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of former 37 CFR 1.60/1.62 continuing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.60 and 1.62 were deleted effective December 1, 1997; continuations/divisionals filed under those former rules on or after that date are treated under current provisions (e.g., 1.53(b) or as RCE under 1.114 depending on circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation or divisional applications filed under former rules prior to Dec 1, 1997 will continue to be processed under prior procedures. Requests for continuation filed under former 1.62 on or after Dec 1, 1997 in certain circumstances will be treated as improper applications or as RCEs; see MPEP references for details.
